question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Travel Account — Author — Route/Region]
options: Itinerario — Jan Huyghen van Linschoten — Portuguese India (Goa)
Description of Arabia — Duarte Barbosa — Arabia and East Africa
Suma Oriental — Tomé Pires — Asia from Red Sea to Japan
Roteiro — Vasco da Gama — First voyage from Lisbon to Calicut
wrong_fact: The Roteiro (journal of Vasco da Gama's first voyage) was written by an anonymous crew member, not by Vasco da Gama himself. It chronicles the route from Lisbon to Calicut 1497–99.
explanation: Jan Huyghen van Linschoten's 'Itinerario' (1596) described Portuguese India from Goa. Duarte Barbosa's 'Description of Arabia' covered Arabia and East Africa. Tomé Pires's 'Suma Oriental' described Asia from the Red Sea to Japan (c.1512–15). The 'Roteiro' was an eyewitness account of Vasco da Gama's first voyage but written by an anonymous sailor, not da Gama himself.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Traveller — Nationality — Primary Region Visited in India]
options: François Bernier — French — Mughal court, Kashmir, Bengal
Niccolao Manucci — Italian — Mughal court, South India
Jean-Baptiste Tavernier — French — Diamond mines of Golconda, Mughal court
Ralph Fitch — Dutch — Bengal, Burma, Malacca
wrong_fact: Ralph Fitch was an English merchant-traveller, not Dutch. He travelled through Bengal, Burma, Malacca and Goa (1583–91) and was one of the first Englishmen to visit India overland.
explanation: François Bernier (French, 1656–68) described the Mughal court and Kashmir. Niccolao Manucci (Italian) spent decades at the Mughal court and in South India. Jean-Baptiste Tavernier (French) made six voyages and described Golconda diamond mines. Ralph Fitch was ENGLISH, not Dutch — he travelled overland through the Levant to India and Southeast Asia, providing early English intelligence on Mughal India.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Travel Account — Geographical Focus — Key Historical Insight Provided]
options: Pires's Suma Oriental — Malabar Coast to Malacca — Spice trade networks and port hierarchies
Linschoten's Itinerario — Goa and coastal India — Portuguese maritime routes and Indian Ocean trade
Barbosa's 'Book' — East Africa, Arabia, India — Pre-Portuguese Indian Ocean commercial world
Pyrard de Laval's Voyage — Maldives, Goa, Bengal — Dutch commercial rivalry with Portugal in Indian Ocean
wrong_fact: François Pyrard de Laval was a French traveller (shipwrecked in Maldives 1602–07), not associated with Dutch commercial rivalry. His account focuses on Maldivian society, Goa's Portuguese administration, and Bengal — not Dutch rivalry.
explanation: Tomé Pires's Suma Oriental is the premier source on spice trade and port hierarchies from Malabar to Malacca (c.1515). Linschoten's Itinerario revealed Portuguese navigation secrets, enabling Dutch and English entry. Barbosa's 'Book' is crucial for understanding the pre-Portuguese Indian Ocean world. Pyrard de Laval (French) provided detailed ethnographic accounts of the Maldives and Portuguese Goa — his work is about French/Portuguese India, not Dutch rivalry specifically.
